title: Abner and Ish-bosheth
lead: Saul's cousin and army commander Abner, and Saul's son Ish-bosheth (Eshbaal), whom Abner made king; Abner changed sides to David and was murdered by Joab, and Ish-bosheth was murdered by his own captains.

sections.b: Abner son of Ner was Saul's cousin (1 Samuel 14:50–51) and commander. He sat beside Saul at table (1 Samuel 20:25) and was mocked by David for failing to guard him (1 Samuel 26:14–16). After Gilboa he made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 2:8–10), whose name appears as Eshbaal in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 8:33; 9:39). Abner killed Asahel in battle (2 Samuel 2:18–23), quarreled with Ish-bosheth over Saul's concubine, offered all Israel to David, and was killed by Joab in the gate of Hebron (2 Samuel 3). David mourned him publicly, and Ish-bosheth was murdered soon after (2 Samuel 4).
